want.now.why: Same order as English, but kwah needs the link word ban before a verb, and ktien (language) carries its marker ka.

want.past.why: Tense is the particle la slipped in between subject and door; kwah itself never changes shape.

want.neg.why: ym fuses onto the pronoun: nga + ym = ngam, one word carrying both subject and negation, in front of the door.

want.q.why: No particle and no inversion: statement order with a rising tone. me is 'you' to a male friend; pha to a female friend, phi to anyone else.

decline.now.why: Both doors (lah, hap) take ban before their verb; namar ba links the clauses and changes nothing after it.

decline.past.why: Past negation adds shym before la (ngam shym la); in speech the second la is often dropped once the past is set.

decline.fut.why: Future yn fuses to the pronoun (ngan) and ym then sits after it, unlike the present where ym fuses instead. lah needs no substitute.

decline.although.why: wat la opens the concession, so the 'although' clause comes first and the main clause follows; each clause keeps subject-door-ban-verb.

like.now.why: The liked thing is an ordinary object, but it takes the object marker ïa and its own gender marker ka.

like.neg.why: Negation is the fused pronoun ngam; nothing else moves and ieid stays the same.

like.she.why: ka is both 'she' and the feminine marker, so the sentence opens and the object begins with the same word. No agreement on the door.

like.q.why: Statement order plus the everyday tag ne em (or not) at the end; rising tone alone also works. me is the informal 'you' to a male friend.

go.habit.why: Bare verb for habit; sha marks direction and the market noun ïew goes without its marker after sha, as in spoken Shillong Khasi.

go.prog.why: Progressive is the particle dang ('in the middle of') before the verb; leit does not change.

go.past.why: la before leit is the whole past tense; English fuses tense into 'went', Khasi keeps it as a separate word.

go.fut.why: Future yn fuses with the pronoun into ngan, so the subject and 'will' are one word; older texts write nga'n.

go.neg.why: Negation fuses onto the pronoun (ngam) and comes before dang, matching the fixed particle order: neg, then aspect, then verb.

live.now.why: The verb stays bare present; lah (already) on the duration does the perfect's job, and 'for' has no word: ar snem is just 'two years'.

live.past.why: Finished period: plain past la before shong. The duration is bare, no preposition.

live.fut.why: Future perfect stacks yn (fused: ngan) and lah before the verb; in speech the lah is often dropped and the time word carries it.

live.q.why: Khasi asks 'since when' (naduh lano) rather than 'how long'; the verb is bare present with no tense particle, and order stays subject-verb.

if.real.why: lada plus the bare verb, then fused future ngan in the result clause. leit kai (go about) is the everyday word for travelling for pleasure.

if.unreal.why: Identical to the real conditional: Khasi has no subjunctive, so unreality comes from context or an adverb; lada tang (if only) can stress it.

if.past.why: Past la in the if-clause, and yn plus la together (ngan la) in the result: the only place Khasi stacks future and past on one verb, meaning 'would have'.
